instructions: Classify all 11 eligible rinse-out products using sections 9 and 10 of the standard.
Do not produce a profile for the excluded leave-in product.
Use the reviewed direct properties for the comparative profile; retain direction evidence separately as protocol metadata. Current catalog fields are not inputs.

Return one complete nine-field comparative profile per eligible product plus concise uncertain_fields and assumption_notes. Exact directions remain protocol metadata rather than comparison properties.

Classify care_direction as protein, moisture, or balanced from the relative prominence of specific protein/peptide routes and humectant/emollient support. This is a product direction, not a user deficiency diagnosis.

Classify repair_support_level as low, medium, or high: ordinary conditioning is low, a distinct temporary protein/peptide film is medium, and a materially stronger paired bond route visible in the reviewed formula is high. Preserve the E2 ceiling and do not treat positioning alone as proof of repair.
Do not add a rinseability projection; weight_potential is the retained ingredient-informed deposition signal.

Apply Damage Fit v1.5: low -> healthy; moderate and general high -> healthy + moderately_damaged. Include highly_damaged only for high conditioning plus a distinct protein/peptide/keratin fibre-film route, named bond chemistry, exceptional corroborated protection, or relevant exact-product test. Generic silicone, oil, panthenol, ceramide, cationic polymer, repair naming, or generic lubrication alone does not qualify.

Return classifications and evidence only. The Lab derives deterministic unsalted per-field fingerprints and owns the one-way v1.4 review-state compatibility bridge; the blind reviewer must not generate or migrate review-state fingerprints.
